name: js-ts-node-async-tests
description: The test skill must load JS/TS validation and testing guidance before running a dependency-free Node suite or strengthening its async assertions. Stage test-files/ as the workspace root outside any SKILL.md ancestor, with Node 24 and npm available. Initialize an empty Git baseline and stage all fixture files as additions so diff-based detection sees the .mjs files.
prompt: Run the existing tests for src/map-values.mjs and strengthen coverage for asynchronous completion, input ordering, rejection propagation, and empty input. Keep the source implementation and existing toolchain unchanged; add no dependencies.
trap: The agent runs npm test before loading profile instructions, leaves floating promise assertions, switches to a familiar framework, or reports the passing Node suite as evidence of type checking or browser coverage.

assertions.text: Agent reads the known profiles' DETECTION.md files and activates only js_ts via .mjs extension signals in the staged workspace.
Agent reads js_ts/test/index.md, validators.md, and testing.md before running any subject-matter validator or changing tests.

Agent checks Node/npm availability, reads package.json, and runs its existing npm test script from the owning package without installing a runner, entering watch mode, or adding flags for another framework.

The revised tests return or await asynchronous work and assertions, assert resolved values in input order even when transformations finish in another order, assert rejection propagation, and cover empty input.
Async ordering is controlled deterministically with promises or explicit synchronization rather than arbitrary sleeps; failures cannot silently pass through unobserved promise chains.
Agent preserves src/map-values.mjs and package metadata, uses the existing node:test and node:assert/strict APIs, and reruns the relevant suite after changing tests.
Agent reports the actual command, scope, and result without claiming a TypeScript check, coverage measurement, or browser test ran when none did.
